author: ribeye
dek: Colleen Hoover's twisty thriller beat Tom Cruise at the box office — and one Springfield book club is taking full credit.
disclaimer: Parody: the Bennett family of Springfield is fictional. The Verity box-office opening is real, as reported by Rotten Tomatoes in October 2026.
headline: Verity Tops the Box Office, and a Springfield Book Club Declares Victory Over Tom Cruise

ohio_quotes.quote: I read the book in two nights and scared myself so badly I slept with the hall light on. Then I dragged my whole family to opening night and made my husband sit in the aisle seat so I could escape if it got too creepy. He has not forgiven me. He also screamed first.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Tara Bennett, Springfield

ohio_quotes.quote: Our book club has been arguing about that manuscript for three years. Three years! And now Anne Hathaway wins the weekend and Tom Cruise gets eight million dollars. I have never felt so vindicated by a spreadsheet.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Mike Bennett, Springfield

ohio_story: SPRINGFIELD, Ohio — Tara Bennett has been telling anyone who would listen — her book club, her neighbors, the cashier at Young's Jersey Dairy — that Colleen Hoover's Verity was going to be huge, ever since she finished the novel in two feverish nights and then immediately made her husband read it too. On Friday, October 2, the movie version opened in theaters, and by Sunday it had done exactly what Tara predicted: it debuted at No. 1 at the box office with $32.6 million, beating Tom Cruise's new film Digger, which managed just $8 million. 'I have been right about exactly one thing in my entire life, and it is this,' Tara said, standing in her driveway in a T-shirt that reads 'I READ THE BOOK.' 'My husband picked Ohio State to lose to Michigan last year. I picked Verity. Look at us now.'

The Bennetts saw the film Friday night as a family, which in practice meant Tara, her husband Mike, and their daughter, who had read the book twice and spent the entire drive to the theater explaining the plot twists to her father, who had not read the book at all and kept saying, 'Wait, the manuscript says what?' Mike, a man who claims he only goes to the movies for the popcorn, was spotted by his own family hiding his eyes during the third act. 'He says he was checking his phone,' Tara said. 'His phone was in the cupholder. I saw it. The whole theater saw it.' Afterward, the family did what Springfield families do after a big night out: ice cream at Young's, where their daughter ranked the movie's twists against the family's all-time list, which currently has the 2014 Ohio State national championship at No. 1 and 'the time Dad got lost driving to the county fair' at No. 2.

By Sunday, the Bennett book club group chat had declared the weekend a historic victory — not just over Tom Cruise, but over every person in Springfield who had ever said, 'It's just a beach read.' Mike has now read the book, finished it in a single Saturday, and has opinions about the ending that he is prepared to defend at Thanksgiving. 'The critics gave it 34%,' he said, scrolling through his phone at the kitchen table. 'Thirty-four. And it still beat Tom Cruise by twenty-four million dollars. I did the math. Twice. That's what happens when you underestimate a book club.'
real_summary: Verity, the psychological thriller directed by Michael Showalter and adapted by Nick Antosca from Colleen Hoover's bestselling 2018 novel, opened in U.S. theaters on October 2, 2026, and debuted at No. 1 at the box office with a $32.6 million opening weekend. Anne Hathaway stars as the incapacitated bestselling author Verity Crawford, alongside Dakota Johnson as Lowen Ashleigh, the ghostwriter hired to finish her books, and Josh Hartnett as her husband Jeremy Crawford.

Critics were not on board with the film — it holds a 34% score on Rotten Tomatoes — but audiences turned out anyway. The $40 million production grossed over $62 million worldwide in its opening weekend, and it became the 19th film to open in October in the $30–40 million range. It was director Michael Showalter's biggest hit to date, surpassing his 2017 Sundance success The Big Sick, which made $42.8 million domestically.

The weekend's other big story was the film Verity beat. Tom Cruise's Digger, an original film from director Alejandro González Iñárritu, opened to just $8 million — the lowest opening weekend for a Cruise headliner since Rain Man ($7 million) in 1988. Behind Verity, Resident Evil took $12.5 million in its third weekend for a $124.8 million domestic total, and Heart of the Beast earned $11 million in its second weekend.
source_note: Rotten Tomatoes box-office report, Oct. 4, 2026: Verity's No. 1 opening weekend, Oct. 2–4, 2026, and Digger's $8 million debut.
